shipped_originals.title_o: Children learn spurious associations in their math textbooks: Examples from fraction arithmetic.

blind_target.authors: Tian, J., Braithwaite, D. W., & Siegler, R. S.
blind_target.title: Distributions of textbook tasks predict student learning: Data from decimal arithmetic.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Our goal was to check whether Swiss

mathematics textbook series may also reveal imbalances in problem frequencies, as

reported by Braithwaite and Siegler (2018) and Tian et al. (2021) for U.S. textbooks.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
These patterns largely resemble, but differ also in part from those observed in U.S.

textbooks, analyzed by Braithwaite and Siegler (2018) and Tian et al. (2021). Most notably

(and to be explicitly tested in Study 2), in Swiss textbooks, children encounter +/- problems

involving fractions with unequal denominators more frequently than those involving equal

denominators. In contrast, U.S. textbooks present these two types of in roughly equal

proportions.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Study 1 confirms nonrandom decimal problem distributions but the authors also explicitly identify important distribution differences from the U.S. textbooks. The new child decimal tasks extend the finding rather than reproduce an original child experiment.
